claims.text: A new potential can be developed that is more accurate than TOR-TILD's EAM references for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The new potential can capture the complex interactions among the multiple principal elements in high-entropy alloys.
Interactions among the multiple principal elements in high-entropy alloys are complex.
An advanced potential can represent both solid and liquid high-entropy material structures near melting.
The new potential will improve the representation of configurations sampled by the ab initio liquid.
Improved configurational representation will increase overlap between the reference and ab initio target phase spaces.
Better reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The new potential will produce less thermodynamic-integration path mismatch than TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed method applies to multicomponent high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states at or near their high melting temperatures.
The method is applicable across composition and temperature ranges relevant to high-entropy alloys.
TOR-TILD's EAM references are the appropriate baseline for evaluating thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
Failure to obtain a significant improvement in configurational representation and reduction in path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references would falsify the hypothesis.
